title: Extension by zero preserves constructibility and Tor amplitude
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ be an
open immersion of
finite-type $k$-schemes, and use the
finite coefficient ring $A$.
For a bounded
constructible complex $K$ of
finite Tor amplitude, its
extension by zero
$j_!K$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Its
cohomological range
and Tor amplitude may be taken to be those of $K$.

proof.text:
Use the finite coefficient stage $A=A_{E,n}$ on the small pro-etale sites of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Here $n\geq1$ and $\ell\neq p$; because all the schemes under consideration are over the field $k$ of characteristic $p$, the image of $\ell$ has an inverse in $k$ and hence in their structure sheaves. Thus the invertibility hypothesis of the finite-level pullback and Tor definitions used below holds. Write $[c,d]$ for any cohomological interval of $K$ and $[a,b]$ for any Tor interval of $K$; these intervals need not coincide. By [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact], $j_!$ is exact. Apply it termwise to a representative $K^\bullet$. Exactness preserves kernels, images and their quotients, so the cohomology description in [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] gives
$$\mathcal H^r(j_!K)=\ker(j_!d^r)/\operatorname{im}(j_!d^{r-1})\cong j_!\bigl(\ker d^r/\operatorname{im}d^{r-1}\bigr)=j_!\mathcal H^r(K).$$
In particular a quasi-isomorphism remains a quasi-isomorphism, so this termwise construction defines extension by zero in the derived category. Since $j_!0=0$, the displayed formula gives vanishing outside $[c,d]$.

source.place: Tag 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact; elementary kernel/image/quotient calculation; blueprint proof paragraph 1, first sentence

proof.text:
The Noetherian-space clause of [def-weil-constructible-subset] applies to the finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$: every subset is retrocompact and every locally closed subset is constructible. In particular, for an affine open $V\subset Y$, $U\cap V$ is quasi-compact. Thus $j$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For each nonzero $F_r=\mathcal H^r(K)$, choose a finite partition $U= igsqcup_
u S_{r,
u}$ witnessing [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Each $S_{r,
u}$ is locally closed in $Y$: by [def-weil-locally-closed-subset], write its image as $O\cap C$ with $O$ open in $U$ and $C$ closed in $U$; write $C=U\cap C'$ for $C'$ closed in $Y$. Since $U$ is open in $Y$, $O$ is open in $Y$, and $S_{r,
u}=O\cap C'$. Give it the same induced locally closed subscheme structure. Adjoining $Z=Y\setminus U$ with its reduced closed subscheme structure yields a finite partition of $Y$ by locally closed constructible subschemes. A separate partition for each $r$ suffices for the definition of constructible cohomology, so no simultaneous refinement theorem is needed.

proof.text:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be the closed immersion from step 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] with $X=Y$ and $R_Y=A_Y$. Its hypotheses hold because $j$ is the complementary quasi-compact open immersion. The constant coefficient identifications and the exact termwise inverse-image interpretation are those of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The cited open-closed statement gives $j^*j_!F_r\cong F_r$ and $i^*j_!F_r=0$ as module sheaves, not merely at ordinary geometric stalks. For the inclusion $s:S_{r,\nu}\to U$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] to $(s,j)$ with constant coefficients, and take degree-zero cohomology. Its compatibility hypothesis on the coefficient identifications holds: direct inverse image along $j\circ s$ and successive inverse image along $j$ and $s$ both send each constant section $a\in A$ to the section with the same value $a$. These sections generate the constant sheaf locally, so the two identifications agree. Exactness of the constant-coefficient inverse images identifies the result with
$$(j\circ s)^*j_!F_r\cong s^*(j^*j_!F_r)\cong s^*F_r.$$
It is the given finite locally constant sheaf on $S_{r,\nu}$. On $Z$ the restriction is the zero sheaf, which is constant with value the finite zero $A$-module. Thus the partition of step 2 witnesses that $j_!F_r$ is constructible by [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Together with step 1 this proves $j_!K\in D^b_c(Y,A)$ with the original cohomological interval $[c,d]$.

proof.text:
Let $M$ be an arbitrary sheaf of $A_Y$-modules in degree zero; it is not assumed constructible. By [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the constant-coefficient pullback is the exact inverse image applied termwise, so $j^*(M[0])=(j^*M)[0]$. The Tor interval hypothesis, in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], therefore gives $\mathcal H^r(K\otimes_A^Lj^*M)=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$. Apply [lem-trf-open-tensor] with $M[0]$ to obtain
$$(j_!K)\otimes_A^LM\cong j_!(K\otimes_A^Lj^*M).$$
By [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact] and the kernel/image/quotient calculation of step 1, the right side has cohomology $j_!\mathcal H^r(K\otimes_A^Lj^*M)$, hence zero for every $r\notin[a,b]$. This holds for every degree-zero module sheaf $M$, so $j_!K$ has Tor amplitude in the same interval $[a,b]$. With bounded constructibility from step 3, [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] gives $j_!K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$.
